title: Oscars: Japan Selects Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s ‘All Of A Sudden’ For International Feature Film Race
full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Ted Hodgkinson To Leave Southbank Centre & Join Hay Festival As Creative Director Janus Films & Criterion Acquire Paul Thomas Anderson’s Cameron Winter Concert Film Oscars: Belgium Selects Lukas Dhont’s ‘Coward’ For International Feature Film Race View All August 26, 2026 2:43am All Of A Sudden CineFrance, Bitters End Ryusuke Hamaguchi ’s latest feature, All Of A Sudden , has been selected as Japan ’s entry for the Best International Feature Film category at the 99th Academy Awards. The Japanese-French-language drama premiered to an 11-minute standing ovation at Cannes and went on to win a Best Actress prize for both of its stars, Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto. Set in France and Japan, All of a Sudden follows Marie-Lou (Efira), the director of a care facility for the elderly, who is determined to introduce an innovative philosophy of care rooted in listening and respect for residents’ dignity, despite resistance from members of her staff. Her path is profoundly reshaped by an encounter with Mari (Okamoto), a Japanese theater director battling cancer. As the two women form a deep friendship, they join forces in a shared struggle to make the impossible possible. Watch on Deadline The film is produced by David Gauquié, Julien Deris, Jean-Luc Ormières and Renan Artukmaç for France’s Cinefrance Studios; Hiroko Matsuda, Kosuke Oshida and Yuji Sadai for Japan’s Office Shirous and Bitters End; Bettina Brokemper for Germany’s Heimatfilm; and Joseph Rouschop for Belgium’s Tarantula. Neon will open the film in theaters on Nov. 25. title: Oscars: Japan Picks Ryusuke Hamaguchi’s ‘All of a Sudden’ as Best Int’l Feature Submission
full_text: × Skip to main content By Patrick Brzeski Plus Icon Patrick Brzeski Asia Bureau Chief View All August 26, 2026 2:39am Tao Okamoto and Virginie Efira in 'All of a Sudden' Cannes Film Festival Japan has selected Ryusuke Hamaguchi ’s luminously cerebral French-language feature All of a Sudden as its submission for the best international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards. The Motion Picture Producers Association of Japan, known as Eiren, announced the choice Wednesday. It marks the second time a Hamaguchi film has represented Japan at the Oscars , following Drive My Car , which was selected five years ago and went on to win best international feature while also earning nominations for best picture, director and adapted screenplay. Related Stories TV Sky Orders "Second Chapter" of Rafe Spall-Starring Crime Drama 'Under Salt Marsh' TV Sky U.K.'s Meghan Lyvers Discusses IP, Original Content Mix and "Increasing the Emotional Stakes" All of a Sudden premiered to acclaim at Cannes in May, where co-stars Virginie Efira and Tao Okamoto shared the best actress prize. The win made Okamoto the first Japanese actress to receive Cannes’ best actress honor. Set largely at a nursing home outside Paris, the film stars Efira as Marie-Lou, the facility’s director, who is attempting to introduce a compassion-based approach to elder care amid chronic understaffing and resistance from some of her employees. A chance encounter brings her into the orbit of Mari (Okamoto), a Japanese theater director with terminal cancer, and the two women form an intense friendship that reshapes both of their lives. In his Cannes review, The Hollywood Reporter ‘s chief film critic David Rooney called All of a Sudden “a work of deeply affecting humanism,” praising its “luminous moments of human connection” and concluding that “the payoff is worth it” despite the film’s three-hour and sixteen-minute runtime. The critical consensus on the Croisette was similarly effusive. As with Drive My Car , All of a Sudden could be a strong multi-category contender at the 99th Academy Awards. Neon, which will release All of a Sudden in the U.S. on Nov. 25, plans to campaign for Efira for best actress and Okamoto for best supporting actress, THR reported Tuesday. The distributor will also push the film for best picture, director and adapted screenplay. Hamaguchi co-wrote All of a Sudden with Léa Le Dimna, drawing loosely from When Life Suddenly Takes a Turn , a best-selling Japanese nonfiction collection of letters between philosopher Makiko Miyano, who was living with terminal cancer, and medical anthropologist Maho Isono. The film is a France-Japan-Germany-Belgium co-production. Hamaguchi, 47, has swiftly become one of Japan’s most internationally decorated filmmakers over the past decade. Along with his Oscar win for Drive My Car , he won Cannes’ screenplay prize for that film, the Silver Bear grand jury prize in Berlin for Wheel of Fortune and Fantasy in 2021 and Venice’s grand jury prize for Evil Does Not Exist in 2023. The 99th Academy Awards will be held March 14, 2027. THR

title: ‘Maserati: The Brothers’ Trailer: Al Pacino, Anthony Hopkins, Jessica Alba and Andy Garcia Star in Motorsport Biopic
full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 26, 2026 2:20am Al Pacino in 'Maserati: The Brothers.' The Andrea Iervolino Company A stellar cast Hollywood stars, including Al Pacino , Anthony Hopkins , Jessica Alba and Andy Garcia feature in the first trailer of Maserati: The Brothers , the motorsport biopic about the family behind the famed Italian car marque. The period film, shot on location in Italy’s automotive capital Modena as well as at Rome’s Cinecittà Studios, tells the story of the Maserati brothers — Alfieri (Michele Morrone), Bindo (Salvatore Esposito) and Carlo (Lorenzo De Moor) — and their attempts to become the first Italian carmaker to win the coveted Indianapolis 500, which the brand famously did in 1939 and 1940. title: Italy’s RAI Cinema International Boards Edoardo De Angelis’ ‘The Fire Within You’ Ahead of Venice Launch, Reveals First Clip (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 26, 2026 2:11am PT Italy’s RAI Cinema International Boards Edoardo De Angelis’ ‘The Fire Within You’ Ahead of Venice Launch, Reveals First Clip (EXCLUSIVE) "I'm fascinated by the misunderstanding surrounding the so-called archetype of the Neapolitan mother," says the director By Nick Vivarelli Plus Icon Nick Vivarelli International Correspondent @NickVivarelli Latest Woody Allen’s New Madrid-Set Movie Comes With Millions in Public Funding — and a Few Strings Attached 17 hours ago Martin Scorsese Appointed Honorary President of Italy’s David di Donatello Academy 21 hours ago ‘NAZA’ Documentary From ‘No Other Land’ Directors Acquired by MK2 Films Ahead of Venice Film Festival Premiere 24 hours ago See All RAI Cinema International Distribution has acquired world rights to Italian director Edoardo De Angelis ‘ dark tragicomedy “The Fire Within You” ahead of its Venice competition launch. De Angelis, a native Neapolitan, broke out on the festival circuit at Venice in 2016 with the Naples-set conjoined twins drama “Indivisible” and subsequently opened the festival in 2023 with anti-war epic “Comandante.” He also directed Netflix’s Elena Ferrante adaptation “The Lying Life of Adults” that year. He will now be back on the Lido vying for the Golden Lion with this more intimate piece, which revolves around the impact a toxic Neapolitan mother has on her progeny. The film is based on the prizewinning autobiographical book “Il fuoco che ti porti dentro” by Italian author and editor Antonio Franchini. Related Stories World Cup Boosts Fox Ad Sales in Q2, Profit Falls 3% “Antonio left Naples many years ago and built a successful career and family life in Milan,” says the film’s synopsis. “He escaped not only from his hometown, but also from his mother Angela, a woman extreme in both her virtues and flaws: irresistible, deeply opinionated, conservative and fiercely confrontational. Now she has arrived for Christmas and seems determined to stay. What begins as a Christmas Eve dinner soon turns into an emotional battlefield, at once comic and merciless, bringing years of misunderstandings, resentment and old wounds to the surface.” The synopsis continues: “A fierce emotional confrontation unfolds between mother and son, but also with a stubborn capon that refuses to end up in the cooking pot; with the anticipation of a daughter who may never arrive; and with a guest as distinguished as he is unexpected. This reckoning between mother and son will forever change the meaning of their relationship. It is a love that burns like an unquenchable fire — one that no distance and no separation can ever extinguish.” “The Fire Within You” is produced by Picomedia, an Asacha Media Group Company that is part of Fremantle, with RAI Cinema. Watch an exclusive first clip from the film above. Below, De Angelis speask to Variety about “The Fire Within You” ahead of the film’s Venice bow. How did “The Fire Within You” originate? The author of the book, Antonio Franchini, is actually a very important editor in Italy. He was following me on the publication of the novel “Comandante,” connected to my film. We had dinner in Naples, and Antonio told me about a book he was writing about his mother. I was immediately fascinated because I found so many similarities with my grandmother and with many women I’ve met in my life. Women who are strong, charismatic, incendiary. He even told me the title and I thought it was very fitting to express the feeling they elicit. Then I read it when it came out and I loved it. But it didn’t cross my mind that it could be made into a film. Then, when I found out that there was a producer who wanted to adapt it into a film, I felt the call of the wild. Because for me, to make a film, all you need is a strong character, like Angela. Obviously, then you have to build everything else. But you can make a film based on that, then the plot can be changed, the story can be rewritten. What does Angela represent for you? Well, first of all, I’m fascinated by the misunderstanding surrounding the so-called archetype of the Neapolitan mother. The Italian mother who is a loving mother, a mother hen who cooks well. See, in this case, her cooking is shit. She hates her children and her grandchildren. In fact, she actually [almost] poisons them with what she cooks. And yet, this type of figure exists in the society that I grew up in: a matriarchal, male-dominated society. That seems like a bit of an oxymoron, but it’s what I grew up with. It’s a human, maternal land of many contradictions. But this type of [toxic] female figure is a widespread archetype even in other places and parts of the world. She’s so strong, it’s devastating. “The Fire Within You” is the fire that Angela carries inside. If you distance yourself from it, you’re nothing. Away from her heat, you freeze to death. If you come too close, you burn. T ell me about working with Vanessa Scalera, who plays Angela . I consider the experience of working with Scalera one of the most rewarding I’ve ever had as a director. At first, we spent days rehearsing and studying each other, because I couldn’t immediately decipher an artist like her. Then there was a moment that became a dividing line. It was when I said: “Vanessa, you’re doing everything really well. But I want something else. I want you to let go; I want you to take me places you don’t even know exist.” Well, right after that, something happened between us on set. I wanted to experience how much the character’s passion pushes her, and she doesn’t even know where this will take her. It’s so strong that it’s like driving a car too fast. You don’t have time to see the road; you don’t see the curves; you’re just going like a madman. Only a crash will stop you. This was the experience of working with Vanessa. And she probably also found some common ground between her personal biography and this character. These are things that, if an actor wants to reveal to me (about themselves) I will keep them, so to speak, in a secret drawer. If she wants to be the one to say this, she will. Or maybe she won’t. But, in short, I have reason to believe that she found some common ground between her biography and this character. Some common ground that allowed her to connect with her movements, mannerisms, attitudes and tics. But none of us really knew where we’d end up. title: Sky Orders “Second Chapter” of Rafe Spall-Starring Crime Drama ‘Under Salt Marsh’
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 26, 2026 2:00am Rafe Spall in 'Under Salt Marsh' Courtesy of Sky Comcast’s Sky unveiled on Wednesday that it has commissioned “the as-yet-untitled second chapter” of original crime drama Under Salt Marsh from creator, writer and director Claire Oakley. Produced by Little Door Productions in association with Sky Studios, the six-part second series sees Rafe Spall reprise his role as the enigmatic Detective Eric Bull. “Following the events of the first [season], Detective Eric Bull (Spall) moves to a remote Scottish mining village sinking under the weight of its own secrets, where a murder investigation brings him closer to the truth about his own past,” reads a plot description. Related Stories TV Sky U.K.'s Meghan Lyvers Discusses IP, Original Content Mix and "Increasing the Emotional Stakes" TV Dominic West and Sienna Miller Star in Image From Sky and HBO Legal Thriller 'War' (Exclusive) Under Salt Marsh launched in January 2026 and became the biggest Sky original drama launch since The Day of the Jackal , as well as Sky’s biggest entertainment title of the year to date, reaching a 28-day audience of 2.5 million. The first season was filmed in Wales and set in the fictional North Wales village of Morfa Halen. “We’re incredibly proud to be returning to the world of Under Salt Marsh with a brilliant new story in Claire Oakley’s distinctive, atmospheric drama,” said Elwen Rowlands, executive producer and CEO of Little Door. “It’s been hugely exciting to see audiences respond to the series’ rich sense of place, complex characters and compelling storytelling. title: Stephen Colbert Urges Emmy Voters to Back Jimmy Kimmel: ‘Look How Cute He Is!’
full_text: Aug 26, 2026 1:52am PT Stephen Colbert Urges Emmy Voters to Back Jimmy Kimmel: ‘Look How Cute He Is!’ By Elsa Keslassy Plus Icon Elsa Keslassy International Correspondent @elsakeslassy Latest Stephen Colbert Urges Emmy Voters to Back Jimmy Kimmel: ‘Look How Cute He Is!’ 36 minutes ago Woody Allen’s New Madrid-Set Movie Comes With Millions in Public Funding — and a Few Strings Attached 17 hours ago Oscars: Belgium Selects Lukas Dhont’s Cannes Prizewinning ‘Coward’ for International Feature Race 21 hours ago See All CBS via Getty Images With Emmy voting drawing to a close, Stephen Colbert has thrown his support behind Jimmy Kimmel in the newly revamped outstanding cariety series race, even though Colbert’s own late-night show is competing in the same category. In a video posted on social media, a bearded Colbert appears sitting outdoors on a windswept coastline with a tablet on his lap, introducing himself while alluding to his recent exit: “Stephen Colbert here, at the end of the world.” Related Stories World Cup Boosts Fox Ad Sales in Q2, Profit Falls 3% View this post on Instagram “You know, there’s 24 hours left in Emmy voting, and if you’re anything like me, you haven’t even started yet. So let’s get going,” Colbert said in the video. Popular on Variety “Kind of a weird voting system this year, but you know, I think we can all agree that Jimmy Kimmel deserves an Emmy,” he continued. “I don’t care if you’ve never even seen his show, you know he deserves an Emmy.” Colbert then flips his tablet and holds it towards the camera, showing a photo of Kimmel: “Besides, look how cute he is! Anyway, please consider thinking that Jimmy deserves an Emmy. I do. I love you.” In endorsing Kimmel, Colbert is returning a favor. Last year, when he was competing against Kimmel for outstanding talk series following CBS’ announcement that it would cancel “The Late Show,” Kimmel mounted his own very public campaign on behalf of his rival. He put up a billboard in West Hollywood featuring himself alongside the message: “I’m voting for Stephen.” Colbert went on to win the category. This year, the two hosts are once again Emmy rivals, though under a very different set of rules. The Television Academy merged the former talk and scripted variety categories into outstanding variety series, whose five nominees are “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” “The Late Show With Stephen Colbert,” “The Daily Show,” “Last Week Tonight With John Oliver” and “Saturday Night Live.” Kimmel also just launched an unconventional — if not daring — Emmy campaign of his own. Rather than showcasing celebrity interviews or standout monologues from “Jimmy Kimmel Live!,” Kimmel assembled a campaign video largely from clips of President Donald Trump repeatedly attacking him and his show. For Colbert, this year’s Emmys come after the end of “The Late Show” in May following an 11-year run on CBS. Its final season earned nine Emmy nominations, including outstanding variety series and outstanding writing for a variety series. Colbert also made a virtual appearance last week to accept the award for outstanding achievement in variety, talk or sketch from the Television Critics Association Awards. The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards are set for Sept. 14. title: ‘Tall Tales & Murder’ First Look: Ella Lily Hyland and Aidan Gillen Star in Wild Comedic Crime Drama From ‘Veep’ Director and ‘Love/Hate’ Creator (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 26, 2026 1:34am PT ‘Tall Tales & Murder’ First Look: Ella Lily Hyland and Aidan Gillen Star in Wild Comedic Crime Drama From ‘Veep’ Director and ‘Love/Hate’ Creator (EXCLUSIVE) The six-part series launches on the BBC later this year By Alex Ritman Plus Icon Alex Ritman @alexritman Latest ‘Tall Tales & Murder’ First Look: Ella Lily Hyland and Aidan Gillen Star in Wild Comedic Crime Drama From ‘Veep’ Director and ‘Love/Hate’ Creator (EXCLUSIVE) 51 minutes ago Paramount’s Brit Network 5 Being Sued by Producer Blackbox Multimedia Over Shelved Drama Series 18 hours ago Anthony Boyle to Lead Sky Drama ‘Charmer’ From Working Title, Story Films 23 hours ago See All BBC Northern Ireland The BBC has lifted the chaotic lid on “Tall Tales and Murder,” its upcoming dark comedic drama from “Love/Hate” creator Stuart Carolan and co-created with Emmy and DGA award winning “ Veep ” director Chris Addison. First announced last year and shot in Ireland, the wild-sounding six-part series mixes what the synopsis describes as a “Bonnie and Clyde style adventure of bent cops, kidnapping, underworld fixers (not to mention libido-enhancing horse medication bootleggers) and the dilemmas of unconventional heroes and villains with an 8th century tall tale of monks, Vikings, buried treasure and a priceless holy book.” Yes, exactly. Related Stories World Cup Boosts Fox Ad Sales in Q2, Profit Falls 3% A co-commission from BBC Northern Ireland and RTÉ in association with Screen Ireland, “Tall Tales and Murder” is produced by Avalon (“Breeders,” ‘Starstruck, “Catastrophe”) in association with Ireland-based Metropolitan Pictures (“Kin”) and will broadcast on BBC One and BBC One Northern Ireland this fall. Popular on Variety In newly-released plot details, the series will follow Bridget, played by Ella-Lily Hyland (“Black Doves,” “Towards Zero”), an unconventional nurse who works the night shift at a Dublin nursing home. She reads the old folk bedtime horror stories, arranges clandestine late night dances and euthanises them if they ask nicely. “Tall Tales & Murder” Mark Sheen But into this secret world comes Paul (Casey Walsh in his first television acting role), a young man stuck stealing cars to repay a debt to crime boss Ma Baker, played by Philippa Dunne (“Amandaland,” “Derry Girls”). Paul is desperate to stay out of prison and needs a legitimate job to keep him safe, so calls on his guardian-angel-of-sorts, an irascible detective called Bunny Ryan, played by Brian Doherty (“Blackshore, Fair City”). Bunny uses his personal history with the Matron of Bridget’s nursing home, played by Aisling O’Sullivan (Raw, The Clinic), to pull in a favour — a favour that will cost him dear. On Bridget and Paul’s first shift together at the nursing home, a mysterious, comatose patient known only as Anonymous, played by Aidan Gillen (“Love/Hate,” “Game of Thrones”), wakes up and reveals he’s the long-lost gangster Grinner McNair, with a buried hoard of Celtic gold. But they’re not the only ones after it — things get complicated as vicious gangster Wesley Swanson, played by Packy Lee (“Peaky Blinders”), and his henchmen close in. “Tall Tales and Murder,” was filmed in the Republic of Ireland and is based on the nine-book “Dublin Trilogy” by Caimh McDonnell. The series was commissioned by David Crean, RTÉ head of drama, and Dermot Horan, RTÉ director of acquisitions & co-productions; and Eddie Doyle, head of content commissioning, and Jason Butler, commissioning editor, for BBC Northern Ireland. Produced by Avalon in association with Metropolitan Pictures, “Tall Tales & Murder” is executive produced by Addison, Richard Allen-Turner, Rob Aslett, Stuart Carolan and Jon Thoday for Avalon, with David McLoughlin and Catherine Tiernan for Metropolitan Pictures. Caroline Norris is series producer, Gemma O’Shaughnessy is producer and the series is directed by Addison and Neasa Hardiman. It will be distributed internationally by Avalon. title: Google DeepMind, Kling AI & Alibaba Join Busan Market’s InnoAsia 2026 Program
full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Lionsgate Strikes Promotional Partnership With Indian Action Star Yash Google DeepMind, Kling AI & Alibaba Join Busan Market’s InnoAsia 2026 Program ReelShort Strikes Microdrama Deal With Indonesian Streamer Vidio For 200 Catalogue Titles & Co-Production Of New Shows View All August 26, 2026 1:18am Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM) Busan International Film Festival Major tech companies including Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services (AWS), Kling AI and Alibaba Group have signed up to participate in the InnoAsia program of this year’s Asian Contents & Film Market ( ACFM ). The official market of Busan International Film Festival, ACFM says it is expanding its scope around the vision of “an innovative ecosystem in which cinema and technology co-evolve.” InnoAsia aims to connect storytelling with emerging technologies, including AI and the rapidly growing microdrama ecosystem. As part of this, ACFM is partnering with global marketing and advertising agency Innocean to co-host the ‘Cinema by Brand 2026’ competition, with the Producers Guild of Korea (PGK) responsible for the selection process and production supervision. Related Stories News YouTube Ad Revenue Rises 13% In Q2 To Surpass $11 Billion, Boosting Parent Alphabet's Performance News A24 Defends Google AI Partnership, Studio Doesn't "Necessarily Love" GenAI Content But "We'd Rather Have A Seat At The Table" Cinema by Brand is described as “an innovative investment and production support platform that connects client brands with film creators worldwide to develop and produce new film content.” Watch on Deadline This year, the competition is seeking 20-minute short film projects featuring Hanwha Group’s ‘Space Solar Power’. The first-round selections will be announced in early September, followed by final pitching in late September, with final selections announced during ACFM. Each selected project will receive production funding, and the selected projects will then be produced and presented to audiences in Korea and worldwide. A session during the market will also explore the significance and potential of branded content in the content business. Meanwhile, in addition to Google, Kling AI and Alibaba, other AI-driven tech companies attending InnoAsia will include BytePlus, Netflix’s VFX studio Eyeline Studios, MegazoneCloud, OPIM Digital, the Korean Film Archive’s VFX asset trading platform i.AM, and InShorts. AI-driven content production companies joining the program include France-based AI/XR content studio Atlas V, Korea’s Mateo AI Studio, MBC C&I, Climax Studio, For Entertainment, K-Dragon and MooAm. Microdrama platforms Mango TV, FlickReels and Vigloo have also confirmed their participation. Kling AI will co-host ‘New Cinematic Possibilities: Reimagining Filmmaking with Kling AI’ and ‘Kling AI Networking Reception: From Production Needs Across Asia to Industry Partnerships’ with ACFM. AWS and MegazoneCloud will launch the ‘AWS Awards’, linked to startup pitching. Winning companies will be selected following a PoC (proof of concept) process and receive AWS cloud vouchers. InnoAsia will also continue its partnerships with international markets, including Berlin film festival’s European Film Market (EFM). Lux AI, an EFM-participating startup developing an intelligent lighting solution for virtual production, and Tanja Meissner, Director Berlinale Pro and EFM, are set to visit Busan. Through collaboration with TAICCA School under the Taiwan Creative Content Agency, imCore, a startup developing an AI solution to improve VFX production efficiency, will also participate. ACFM and InnoAsia 2026 are taking place October 10-13 at the BEXO exhibition centre, during Busan International Film Festival, which is running October 6-15. title: Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 26, 2026 1:09am PT Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE) By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Oscars: Japan Selects ‘All of a Sudden’ for International Feature Race 2 hours ago Vidio Teams With ReelShort for First Indonesian Short-Drama Partnership 3 hours ago See All DRX/Nuon Korea’s DRX Corp. and PT Nuon Digital Indonesia signed a strategic partnership in Jakarta to expand gaming and entertainment ties between Indonesia and Korea, starting with an entertainment festival called DRX Homefront Indonesia and a joint game publishing initiative between the two countries. The agreement pairs DRX’s esports, content production and fan engagement experience with Nuon’s local distribution network, creator relationships and knowledge of the Indonesian market. The two companies plan to start by exploring three areas: live entertainment, game publishing and talent development. Indonesia’s population of more than 280 million, its mobile-first consumer base and its appetite for Korean entertainment make it a market both companies pointed to directly in unveiling the deal. Popular on Variety “Indonesia is an important market for the future of entertainment in Asia,” said Can Yang, CEO of DRX. “Success in this market requires more than bringing an international brand to local audiences. It requires the right local knowledge, relationships and execution. Working with Nuon gives us the opportunity to develop experiences that reflect what Indonesian audiences want while creating stronger connections with Korea’s entertainment industry.” The companies will explore developing DRX Homefront Indonesia as a flagship festival in Jakarta built around gaming and entertainment, drawing in players, fans and creators from both countries. Plans on the table include competitive gaming showcases, community programs for creators, fan meet-ups and concert-style shows featuring K-pop acts. On the publishing side, the partnership will look at bringing select Korean game titles into Indonesia while helping Indonesian-developed games reach Korea. That would put DRX and Nuon in charge of everything from picking titles and adapting them for the local market to marketing, signing up players, getting the games into stores and handling payments. The companies also plan to bring pieces of DRX’s existing academy setup to Indonesia, with organized coaching, camps held in Korea and routes for Indonesian players to break into the region’s pro gaming circuit. “Indonesia’s growing gaming and digital entertainment ecosystem presents significant opportunities for collaboration with leading players from Korea,” said Chandra Tamrin, director of Nuon. “Through this partnership with DRX, we aim to connect the strengths of both markets – bringing new gaming and entertainment experiences to Indonesian audiences while creating pathways for Indonesian games, talent and creative opportunities to reach the Korean and broader regional market. This collaboration reflects our commitment to continuously expanding Indonesia’s digital entertainment ecosystem through international partnerships.” DRX and Nuon plan to form a joint team to map out their initial projects and how the rollout will work, with more specifics expected once those plans come together. The Nuon deal extends a broader push DRX has been making beyond its esports roots. The company recently detailed plans to move into K-dramas and game publishing through its subsidiary WebsCreative, including agreements around two unannounced, fully cast K-drama projects with major Korean broadcasters. Yang has described the goal as building DRX into a digital entertainment company that keeps esports as one pillar among several, with Southeast Asia named as a priority region for that growth – a strategy the Jakarta signing puts into practice. Ted Hodgkinson, the Southbank Centre ’s longtime director of literature and spoken word, is leaving the London institution to join Hay Festival in the newly created role of creative director. Hodgkinson will officially join the Hay Festival team in the autumn. In the new role, Hodgkinson will be responsible for leading the event’s artistic and creative strategy and public programming. He joins Hay’s executive team, led by Chief Executive Julie Finch. The wider executive team also includes International Director and co-Deputy CEO, Cristina Fuentes La Roche; Executive Producer and co-Deputy CEO, Adrian Lambert; Director of Communications and External Affairs, Christopher Bone; Finance Director Amanda Cartwright; Production Director Georgie Cooke; and Commercial Director Penny Compton. title: Sky U.K.’s Meghan Lyvers Discusses IP, Original Content Mix and “Increasing the Emotional Stakes”
full_text: × Skip to main content By Georg Szalai Plus Icon Georg Szalai Global Business Editor View All August 26, 2026 1:00am Meghan Lyvers, managing director, scripted originals, Sky U.K. Courtesy of Sky Comcast’s Sky recently showed its desire to grow via an acquisition, agreeing to acquire ITV’s networks and streaming businesses in a $2.13 billion deal. But the company has also been growing its investment in original content in recent years to ensure it can regularly premiere attractive series and films for its subscribers in a competitive industry where streamers and traditional players constantly tout new and returning programming. Sky has been betting on series that it feels can break through in this environment. Case in point: the upcoming October premiere of legal drama War , whose first of two seasons, ordered together with HBO, stars Sienna Miller and Dominic West . Or how about season 2 of Sweetpea , the dark comedy starring Ella Purnell ( Fallout , Yellowjackets ) as a wallflower-turned-killer, which returns to Sky in November, before partner Starz airs it next year. Sky audiences have this year already been able to watch the likes of Possession, the limited inheritance mystery series led by Gugu Mbatha-Raw ( Loki) , and Prisoner , the high-speed action series starring Izuka Hoyle, which has been renewed for a second season . Related Stories TV Dominic West and Sienna Miller Star in Image From Sky and HBO Legal Thriller 'War' (Exclusive) Movies Netflix Sets Lee Jung-eun, Kim Moo-yul for Korean Action-Noir Series 'The Shooter' Plus, early this year, Sky had success with the Rafe Spall-starring Under Salt Marsh , which it just renewed for season 2, and it has unveiled an eight-episode “bold and contemporary reimagining [that] brings The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo into the present, grounded in the characters and investigative DNA of Stieg Larsson’s Millennium novels, with themes that carry heightened relevance today.” All in all, Meghan Lyvers, managing director, scripted originals, Sky U.K., is clearly keeping busy. The executive first joined Sky in late summer 2022 and relocated from Amsterdam to London, reporting to Cécile Frot-Coutaz , who is chief advertising and content officer at Sky and CEO of Sky Studios. Her remit has since been expanded . Lyvers previously served as senior vp and head of international co-productions and development at CBS Studios after working as a producer at Management 360. She began her career at Robert De Niro and Jane Rosenthal’s Tribeca Productions with such projects as About a Boy and the Meet the Parents franchise. On Wednesday afternoon, Lyvers will be featured during a “Spotlight on Sky” session at the Edinburgh TV Festival , along with fellow commissioners Philip Edgar-Jones, executive director, unscripted originals, Sky U.K., and Sky managing director, programming Jamie Morris. Ahead of her Edinburgh appearance, Lyvers talked to THR about her team’s original content strategy, why ambition and characters are key, Sky’s film slate and how important, or not, franchises and star power are. How do you approach your commissioning strategy for and what is key for content to get your and your team’s attention? Our North Star is the audience. We’re a premium pay service, and the Sky audience has so many options. Between sport and the entertainment offering, we also acquire a lot of content still from the U.S. So if you think about the Sky audience, if you have that subscription, it’s got to be exceptional when it comes to original programming. It has to be exceptional, complementary programming, whether that’s unscripted or scripted. I look after the scripted group, for film and series for TV, and talking about it with our commissioning teams, [it’s about] what’s the most ambitious, most provocative, most character-driven story? Do you have targets for how many originals you premiere, or is it more about quality? I’ve worked in other places where you have more volume, and you have to do a lot of different things. But we get to be super-curated and think about what those stories are that are going to be really bold and provocative and really stay with the audience and impact them in a deeply emotional way. We don’t make a huge amount of volume, although our investment is going up, which is fantastic because the business is like, “Hey, what you’re doing is great. Let’s keep building!” So, we really do think about what are the most provocative and ambitious stories we can tell. Colin Firth in ‘Lockerbie: A Search for Truth.’ Sky Studios/Peacock How do you think about the mix of big returnable shows and one-offs? Strategically, in terms of how we program, we always make limited series. So, last year we did Lockerbie: A Search for Truth with Colin Firth, which was incredible. We just launched a limited series this month called Possession with Gugu Mbatha-Raw, which is amazing. It’s a really provocative story [about the horrors of colonialism], and also thematically something that we thought we have to tell because it’s still relevant, no one’s doing this, and we can do it. Let’s back ourselves. Let’s do something that we think is going to create a very specific and important and relevant conversation. So, limiteds are always going to be something that we do as a big global story that captures a conversation and feels relevant to our audiences in the U.K. And then, of course, we really like to make a couple of big, massive, often IP-based, franchises. The Day of the Jackal is a really great example. I’ve just seen a couple of cuts of [season] 2, and it’s going to be fantastic. We can’t wait to bring that back next year. In that tradition, we want to make more franchises, which is hard because it’s like making studio films on steroids. It’s really complicated. They take a ton of time to prep. They’re massive stories. They have huge production value. The footprint of locations and shooting is massive. But we’re making the next one, which is The Girl With the Dragon Tattoo , and that’s coming up in terms of the shoot, so we will be talking about it more. It’s our next franchise series that we hope will run for more than one [season]. It’s a wonderful, faithful way in which we pay respect to the IP and legacy of those books, which I devoured and loved. But it also takes the Swedish films and David Fincher’s film and evolves the story for today. You’d be surprised how much, thematically, it still resonates. So if you’re a fan of the books, if you’re a fan of the series, if you’re a fan of the films, if you love what’s inside of this, you have something new to explore. We have been asked to make one to two of those a year. So that’s our next one that we’re excited about. You have also been championing British stories. What can you share about those? We would like you to make more of these contemporary British stories about British characters in different genres. Under Salt Marsh was our version of doing a really smart, very character-driven, emotional crime story. It had a propulsive murder mystery in it, but it felt so different – something that you couldn’t get anywhere else. You wouldn’t see that on a streamer. You wouldn’t see it on a public broadcaster. And that’s for us. Let’s push ourselves to make that story as ambitious as possible, in the storytelling, but also in the execution, and make it feel completely authored. [Importantly,] those characters, at the end of the day, are relatable, and that’s something where we have really listened to our audiences the last couple of years. So we’re making more of those because viewers tell us that they want them, but they also perform extremely well. Ella Purnell in ‘Sweetpea.’ Courtesy of Starz We get the feedback from audiences that they enjoy the characters and the storytelling, and it’s propulsive, and it looks gorgeous, but they also are saying that these stories connect with me as a viewer. So it is something for us to continue to build on. The [same goes for] Prisoner and Sweetpea , which does this in a very genre way. And our next one coming up is Charmer , led by Anthony Boyle . So, you have limited series and returning franchises – anything else worth highlighting for the original content mix? The last piece is that we’ll make one provocative, bold, really edgy show that is completely character-driven. Last year, we made a show with Matt Smith and Clerkenwell Films called The Death of Bunny Munro , based on the Nick Cave novel. I couldn’t make that anywhere else. The fact that Sky lets us and our audience program those originals, and that they have been received so well, is a pleasure. You mentioned the importance of authorship. Tell me a bit more about that, please. Claire Oakley, who is a filmmaker, created, wrote and directed Under Salt Marsh . She had a story she wanted to tell, and we were like: “We have to make this.” And because Claire wanted to tell a story that was climate-adjacent, it does speak to a very specific community being impacted by this thing in a way that feels very organic. All the climate stories in this show are part of the desire to be authentic, but also speak to what our audiences are living through. So, it’s about finding stories that also really hook and engage audiences? Yeah, it’s not just about making great shows with exceptional production value if they are lacking emotion. I started in film, where it’s always been about the character and the point of view of that character. With TV, you need to make sure that the audience feels an emotional connection to those characters. We talked very openly about making sure that our shows continue to have wonderful execution that everyone in the industry and customers know from Sky, which means you’re going to see something that looks epic and on par with rivals and the Hollywood studio systems. But what we also wanted to do was make sure we increase the emotional stakes, and so the audience feels a more a stronger personal connection to the characters and what those characters are going through. So it’s about big emotions. If we’re not going to make a ton of shows, all of our shows have to really impact the audience. TV viewing is instinctual. There’s a gut instinct that you can’t deny. If you emotionally connect to something, you’re going to watch it, and you’re going to talk to your friends about it, and you’re going to be passionate about it, and you’re going to want a [season] 2 to come back. Eddie Redmayne in ‘The Day of the Jackal.’ NBCUniversal You have been working with production companies and distribution partners, such as HBO and Starz, on originals. The upcoming War seems to be an example of how Sky works with different outside and inside partners. Sky gave the series a two-season order, with HBO/HBO Max taking it for the U.S. and Australia, and NBCUniversal , which Sky is a part of, distributing it internationally. How do you approach partnerships? We really like to work with a bunch of different partners. We’re really proud that we can work with somebody like Carnival Films, which is in our bigger corporate family [of NBCUniversal], and they do incredible work – whether it’s on Lockerbie or Jackal . But we are also working with Little Door Productions [in Cardiff], an incredible opportunity to support this small production company that’s in Wales that has this incredible story to be told. Do you have any qualitative targets, a la how many originals you make, and do you target audience segments or so? What I can say is that at Sky, we don’t have an algorithm. So we still make human decisions, and ideas must pass our gut check of “would we watch this”? We definitely need to make sure that our bigger tentpole shows that have huge investments, for example, The Day of the Jackal , appeal to bigger audiences. So we do think about broadening those. But I think the fun part of making shows like Bunny Munro or or even Possession is that we get to make shows that are much more singular. And if they grow, it’s because people love them and there’s word of mouth and it creates zeitgeist. You have shows with Sienna Miller and Dominic West , or Ella Purnell. How do you guys think about the need for star power? I’ll say this: look, we don’t have talent deals. Those shows have to be good enough on the page for an actor like Dominic or Sienna to say, “I have to play this part. I’m obsessed with this character. I love this script.” It’s the same way with Anthony Boyle with Charmer. He fell in love with the script. So for us, it starts with the material, what’s on the page, and no doubt, well-established actors help bring an audience to a show. But we have a lot of other means in which we can bring audiences into shows via the marketing campaigns and social. We make sure that the actor is right for the role and they have to love it. Rafe Spall in ‘Under Salt Marsh’ Courtesy of Sky Existing IP is obviously also a way to get an audience’s attention right away. You have mentioned Jackal and Dragon Tattoo . Anything you can add on that front? No doubt, when you talk to people all over the industry about this, it’s really important to have a mix of stories. Original ideas still cut through. Under Salt Marsh was 100 percent Claire Oakley’s original idea. Prisoner was an original idea. Possession is an original idea. For us, it’s continuing to find the right balance because our audiences really like to see a bit of both. So, we believe in the mix, and because we don’t make a huge volume, it’s really about getting that balance right. Any goals for Sky’s original output and budget sizes ahead that you can mention? It’s not formulaic. Our investment is going up. So, 2029 is going to be our biggest year in terms of overall investment in scripted originals for series, and then we talk about what is the right budget size for each particular show. That’s where things differ between [comedy] Mr Bigstuff and, say, [drama] Meantime , which is coming up next year with James McAvoy, or Jackal , because these stories all need something different. So, we take more of an approach of what’s the right budget for the show, and look at the factors of how the budget gets split across the year. Jason Statham and Annabelle Wallis in ‘Mutiny.’ Dan Smith/Lionsgate Before I let you go, what can you tell us about Sky’s original film strategy? It’s a wonderful pleasure for me to look after the film group because we have had such an incredible run. If you think about Nuremberg , [the star-studded character piece about the Nuremberg Trials] last year, for example, or Kate Winslet with Lee , [in which she starred as the pioneering World War II photojournalist Elizabeth “Lee” Miller]. We had [British crime thriller] Fuze earlier this year and just launched Mutiny with Jason Statham. For us, on the film side, it’s really important that we continue to support the British filmmaking community. For example, we’re going to debut Animol , which is Ashley Walter’s directorial debut , later this year. Seeing an actor turn to directing or producing, it’s just such a pleasure to be able to support them in their storytelling journeys. THR

title: Netflix’ Latest Marketing Mash-Up Pairs Stella Artois With ‘The Gentlemen’
full_text: Aug 26, 2026 1:00am PT Netflix’ Latest Marketing Mash-Up Pairs Stella Artois With ‘The Gentlemen’ By Brian Steinberg Plus Icon Brian Steinberg Senior TV Editor bristei Latest Netflix’ Latest Marketing Mash-Up Pairs Stella Artois With ‘The Gentlemen’ 2 hours ago Emily Compagno Joins Fox News’ ‘The Five’ as Co-Host 2 days ago Roku Names Gianluca Pucacco VP, Revenue Operations, International Growth 2 days ago See All Matthew Towers/Netflix Netflix has what looks to be a great show set to launch, but you can’t see the program on its flagship streaming service. The company plans to take over the history Marlborough Pub in London between September 3 and September 5, when it will outfit the place much like its comedic action series “The Gentlemen,” which is about to launch its second season. At the pub, visitors will be able to look for hidden messages from the show, which is created by Guy Ritchie, order a Stella Artois , and take home limited-edition merchandise including their an engraved chalice. The partnership, which will also include a series of vignettes outlining a five-step pouring ritual associated with the Anheuser-Busch InBev brew, marks the first brand alliance for the series, and the first execution in a multi-year deal struck between the brewing giant and the streaming titan, initially unveiled in September of last year. Popular on Variety Wrapping Stella Artois in the trappings of the series was key to the alliance, says Marcel Marcondes, global CMO of Anheuser Busch InBev, via email. “We didn’t want to place the brand alongside the story,” he says. “We wanted to it feel so integrated that fans wouldn’t be able to distinguish between the content and the show.” The video vignettes will feature series star Theo James as well as soccer great David Beckham, who has served as a brand ambassador for the beer since 2024. Netflix has worked assiduously to burnish its reputation as a home for advertisers seeking to align themselves with its popular programs and eager to avoid the traditional model of deploying typical 30-second commercials. Netflix in 2019 was able to convince Coca-Cola to revive New Coke, a failed revamp of its flagship product — all because the beverage was featured in the third season of “Stranger Things.” The streamer has put a spotlight on its ability to create bespoke alliances with its programs, according to media buyers who have negotiated ad deals with the company, realizing that such offerings might entice advertisers to buy more regular commercial inventory. Earlier this year, Netflix pushed the marketing-industry envelope by weaving popular State Farm spokes-character Jake from State Farm into the plot of its sports series “Running Point.” “We’re really excited about how this partnership came to life. It’s a true piece of entertainment that extends ‘The Gentlemen’ beyond the screen, that we know fans around the world are going to love,” says Magno Herran, vice president of global brand and marketing partnerships at Netflix, via email. “‘The Gentlemen; checks all the right boxes,” he adds. “It’s a show that our fans love globally, with a touch of real British style and swagger that pairs incredibly well with a brand like Stella Artois. It offered the perfect place for a brand and the story to come together in a way we couldn’t do individually.” The team-up between brewer and streamer will be seen in the U.S., the U.K., Canada, Brazil, Colombia, Mexico, South Africa and South Korea. The bet is that the interesting content will entice fans around the world and grow the series’ audience as the debut of its second season draws near. Social-media feeds controlled by Netflix or Stella Artois will also boost the alliance. title: Oscars: Japan Selects ‘All of a Sudden’ for International Feature Race
full_text: Aug 26, 2026 12:39am PT Oscars: Japan Selects ‘All of a Sudden’ for International Feature Race By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE) 1 hour ago Oscars: Japan Selects ‘All of a Sudden’ for International Feature Race 2 hours ago Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services, Kling AI Join Busan Market Tech Program InnoAsia 3 hours ago See All Courtesy of Neon, Cannes Film Festival Hamaguchi Ryusuke ‘s “ All of a Sudden ” has been selected as Japan’s entry in the international feature category at the 99th Academy Awards, the Motion Picture Producers Association of Japan (Eiren) has revealed. The selection marks the second time a Hamaguchi film has represented Japan in the category, five years after “Drive My Car” won the international feature Oscar and picked up nominations for best picture, director and adapted screenplay at the 94th Academy Awards. Related Stories World Cup Boosts Fox Ad Sales in Q2, Profit Falls 3% “All of a Sudden” is a France-Japan co-production made with backing from Germany and Belgium, shot largely in Paris. The film draws on “When Life Suddenly Takes a Turn: Twenty Letters Between a Philosopher With Terminal Cancer and a Medical Anthropologist,” a book of correspondence by Miyano Makiko and Isono Maho. It follows Marie-Lou Fontaine (Virginie Efira), who runs a nursing home outside Paris and pushes to adopt a more dignity-focused model of elderly care, and Morisaki Mari (Okamoto Tao), a Japanese theater director undergoing cancer treatment. Nagatsuka Kyōzō and Kurosaki Kōdai round out the cast. Popular on Variety The film premiered in competition at the Cannes Film Festival in May, where it drew a seven-minute standing ovation . Efira and Okamoto shared the festival’s best actress prize; Okamoto is the first Japanese performer to win it. “All of a Sudden” opened in Japan on June 19 through Bitters End. Diaphana Distribution released the film in France on Aug. 12, and Neon will open it in North American theaters on Nov. 25. Eiren’s pick now advances to the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, which will winnow submissions from countries around the world down to a shortlist of 15 films before narrowing to five nominees. The 99th Academy Awards ceremony will take place March 14, 2027. title: ReelShort Strikes Microdrama Deal With Indonesian Streamer Vidio For 200 Catalogue Titles & Co-Production Of New Shows
full_text: Skip to main content By Liz Shackleton Liz Shackleton pmc-media-editor-2024 More Stories By Liz Lionsgate Strikes Promotional Partnership With Indian Action Star Yash Google DeepMind, Kling AI & Alibaba Join Busan Market’s InnoAsia 2026 Program ReelShort Strikes Microdrama Deal With Indonesian Streamer Vidio For 200 Catalogue Titles & Co-Production Of New Shows View All August 26, 2026 12:08am Rahasia Kelam Kakak Tiriku Vidio ReelShort has struck a deal with Indonesian streaming platform Vidio to bring hundreds of microdramas to local audiences, as well as co-produce new short dramas with Indonesian production houses. ReelShort catalogue titles will be available on Vidio starting on September 1 through the dedicated Short Drama tab, launched by Vidio last year, for subscribers on the TV Extra, Platinum, Platinum Extra, and Ultimate packages. The initial offering will include more than 200 titles across popular genres including romance, billionaire romance, fantasy and family drama, with a wide selection of titles available with Indonesian dubbing and subtitles. Related Stories News International Insider: Australia's Attention Battle; Vertical Video Rises; Kevin Macdonald On Pep Guardiola News FlareFlow & Europe's Shorts Strike Four-Title Microdrama Pact In addition, a “sizable” slate of short drama series co-produced with Indonesian production houses will be made available across both platforms. In a statement, Vidio said the collaboration “creates opportunities for Indonesian creative talent to gain production expertise and knowledge from ReelShort’s global short-drama experience”. Watch on Deadline The partnership, brokered by AR Global Media Network, is ReelShort’s first in Indonesia and is part of a wider expansion across Southeast Asia that has also included strategic partnerships with AIS in Thailand and Globe in the Philippines. According to recent data from Media Partners Asia (MPA), ReelShort currently leads the short-form drama market with an estimated 29% global market revenue share. In Q2 2026, Vidio reached 5.8 million paid subscribers across Southeast Asia, ranking third regionally. MPA data also shows that Indonesia has emerged as Asia-Pacific’s largest market for short-form drama consumption, accounting for 39% of the region’s total audience. Sutanto Hartono, CEO of Vidio, said: “Vidio continues to evolve alongside the changing ways Indonesians consume entertainment. As audiences increasingly look for content that fits seamlessly into their daily lives, we want to ensure they can find every type of entertainment they love on a single platform, from live sports, local originals, global entertainment to now, the rapidly growing format of short dramas. “Our partnership with ReelShort not only responds to this emerging audience demand but also strengthens Vidio’s position as Indonesia’s most comprehensive entertainment platform, offering more choice, greater convenience, and an even richer viewing experience for our subscribers.” Joey Jia, Founder and CEO of Crazy Maple Studio, owner of ReelShort, said: “Our partnership with Vidio marks a significant milestone in ReelShort’s Southeast Asia growth strategy and reflects a fundamental shift in how audiences are consuming entertainment. “Indonesia is one of the region’s most dynamic entertainment markets. We see tremendous potential not only to expand access to our global catalogue, but also to create original stories for Indonesian audiences. Through our planned local productions with Vidio and Indonesian production partners, we look forward to combining ReelShort’s global experience in developing high-performing short-drama IP with local creative talent to build stories and franchises that resonate locally while reaching audiences across the region and beyond.” Lionsgate Inks Partnership With Indian Action Star Yash Tributes, Career Gallery & Obituary For Music, Humanitarian Icon Ryan Gosling And WB Eye Live-Acton ‘Flintstones’ Pic About Bamm-Bamm ‘Bel-Air’ Spinoff ‘Hilary’ Starring Coco Jones In Works At Peacock Read More About: Comments

title: ‘Ted Lasso’ Stars Juno Temple & Hannah Waddingham Detail Firework Scene They Were “Chomping At The Bit “ To Do In Season 4
full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Dolly Parton: Beyoncé, Pedro Pascal, Sabrina Carpenter & More Pay Tribute To “One Of One” Country Music Legend HBO Sets ‘The Gilded Age’ Season 4 Premiere Date; Unveils Teaser Everything We Know About Amazon MGM & Sony Pictures TV’s ‘God Of War’ Adaptation So Far View All August 26, 2026 12:01am L-R: Juno Temple and Rebecca Waddingham in ' Ted Lasso' Season 4 Apple TV SPOILER ALERT: This post spoils Ted Lasso Season 4 Episode 4 , titled “Greyhounds’ Day Off.” Getting a women’s soccer team off the ground takes its challenges, which Keeley Jones ( Juno Temple ) and Rebecca Welton ( Hannah Waddingham ) have begun to realize four episodes into the fourth season of Ted Lasso . From the “Higgins Report” disclosing some devastating numbers and probabilities about whether the team could profit to their different mindsets of going about business, the pair have clashed over decisions. Rebecca has had to say no to many a Keeley pitch, and Keeley has, in turn, had to get creative. Related Stories News All The Songs In ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 So Far News Meet The Lady Greyhounds: Key Players & Staff For AFC Richmond’s Women’s Team In ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 In Episode 4, Keeley’s eagnerness is on full display when she and Rebecca witness Zelda Southport (Tracy Ullman) speak at a conference. Rebecca’s desire to remain demure and not show their cards wins out, and she ends up googling Zelda and finding some red flag results. Rebecca accidentally calls Keeley “naïve” after the publicist and burgeoning businesswoman wants to enlist Zelda in their mission of getting the women’s team more funding and attention, but the pair make up in the Nelson Road stadium seats one night. Watch on Deadline “We were chomping at the bit to go into that scene, weren’t we?” Waddingham said of the reconciliation between the female friends. “Totally. It’s so interesting when I think about that now. We didn’t even have to talk about what it was. We just had to run our lines together” Temple added. “Which is such an interesting and a beautiful thing to be able to say.” Complete with pink fuzzy blankets and thermos mugs, Rebecca apologizes and voices how she feels bad that she has to shut down many of Keeley’s ideas, but Keeley takes it in stride and says it’s okay, embracing the way it makes her think of another way to “get things done.” @deadline #JunoTemple on the transformation of Keeley’s style throughout #TedLasso ♬ original sound – Deadline “We played it, and then we had to go back over it because it was Diwali when we were shooting it, and so we were really shut down by the fireworks,” Waddingham continued, with Temple chiming in that they “weren’t supposed to actually pay attention to” the pyrotechnics. The distracting Diwali fireworks distracted led to reshoots of the pivotal moment. “You were guilty of this too. I won’t let that slide,” Temple said in response to her costar. “I kept being distracted because I’m like Keeley. I like anything that glitters, that’s sparkly, and I kept looking at them, then being like, “Oh my god, they’re not supposed to be there.’” In the show, Keeley has also tasked Kenneth the Bus Driver (Mark Kempner), who sources drugs and now, fireworks, apparently, to test out different hues of the colorful smoke that is popularly used opening women’s soccer games. The explosions provide different interruptions, punctuating the moment as one of Keeley’s ideas plays out in real time.

title: Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services, Kling AI Join Busan Market Tech Program InnoAsia
full_text: Aug 26, 2026 12:00am PT Google DeepMind, Amazon Web Services, Kling AI Join Busan Market Tech Program InnoAsia By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Oscars: Japan Selects ‘All of a Sudden’ for International Feature Race 2 hours ago Vidio Teams With ReelShort for First Indonesian Short-Drama Partnership 3 hours ago See All Busan ACFM The Asian Contents & Film Market (ACFM), the market of the Busan International Film Festival , will present InnoAsia 2026, its program built around the intersection of film and emerging technology. This year’s participants include Amazon Web Services (AWS), Kling AI, Google DeepMind and Alibaba Group, alongside a range of other technology and content companies and startups. The program is built around a vision of cinema and technology developing side by side, with a scope that runs from brand-film partnerships to the fast-growing microdrama business. Related Stories YouTube Creator Kevin Langue Is Bringing His Comedy Channels to Netflix Netflix, AMC Team for 'Bannerman' Series Based on John R. Maxim Spy Novels, Shane Black and Craig Silverstein to Write ACFM and global marketing agency Innocean will co-host Cinema by Brand 2026, a new competition with the Producers Guild of Korea handling selection and production oversight. The platform links brand clients with filmmakers around the world to turn advertising messages into standalone films with real narrative ambition, rather than conventional commercials. This year’s contest calls for 20-minute short films built around Hanwha Group’s “Space Solar Power.” First-round picks arrive in early September, followed by final pitching later that month, with winners named during ACFM. Selected teams get production funding and will see their films shown to audiences in Korea and abroad. A market session will dig into what branded content means for the business and how the initiative came together, with participation expected from Hanwha, Innocean and the selected directors. Popular on Variety Beyond brands and filmmakers, InnoAsia is deepening ties with technology firms and international markets. This year’s AI-driven tech participants include AWS, Google DeepMind, BytePlus, Alibaba Cloud, Netflix’s VFX studio Eyeline Studios, MegazoneCloud, OPIM Digital, the Korean Film Archive’s VFX trading platform i.AM, Kling AI and Inshorts. On the content-production side, France’s Atlas V joins Korea’s Mateo AI Studio, MBC C&I, Climax Studio, For Entertainment, K-Dragon and MooAm, while microdrama platforms Mango TV, FlickReels and Vigloo round out the roster. Kling AI will co-host two sessions with ACFM, New Cinematic Possibilities: Reimagining Filmmaking with Kling AI and a networking reception tied to production needs across Asia. AWS and MegazoneCloud will launch new AWS Awards linked to startup pitching, with winners chosen through a proof-of-concept process and awarded AWS cloud vouchers. On the international side, EFM-linked startup Lux AI, which builds intelligent lighting tools for virtual production, will travel to Busan along with Tanja Meissner, director of Berlinale Pro and EFM. Through a partnership with TAICCA School under the Taiwan Creative Content Agency, VFX-efficiency startup imCore will also take part. Seven Korean startups were chosen through an open call run with the Busan Center for Creative Economy & Innovation and AWS, together spanning the full content pipeline. On the development and production side, Lumicraft’s AI casting tool Castlink pairs actor discovery with contracting and settlement, while Reproduction’s Pre-Flow handles screenplay analysis and production data sharing. For localization, Voithru’s Totus offers AI dubbing across 29 languages, and XL8 brings both MediaCAT and EventCAT for video localization and real-time interpretation. On the exhibition side, Digion Cinema will show off an online cinema platform and AR smart glasses built for film viewing. MyStarChain will present its blockchain voting platform MyStarPick, and HiStranger will introduce Insight Flow, a tool that reads biosignals to gauge audience emotional response. InnoAsia 2026 will run several programs across three tracks: technology proof-of-concept and investment, creators and production, and industry and policy. The InnoAsia Startup Demo Jam sits at the center of the first track, with nine companies, drawn from the open call and international partner recommendations, pitching AI, virtual production and digital-asset technologies to investors and buyers. The InnoAsia WIP Showcase will preview AI-based features, animation, series and interactive projects from directors including Pierre Zandrowicz, Mark Wachholz and Kang Yunsung, paired with a colloquium on AI production pipelines. A Cinematic AI conference will spotlight Google DeepMind’s AI animation work and an AI film from director Darren Aronofsky, both previously featured at Cannes Next, and will examine AI filmmaking ecosystems with input from Alibaba Cloud and Kling AI. AI Creators Camp offers hands-on workshops led by VFX supervisors from major studios and creators who have won at AI film festivals. On the policy side, a panel titled Microdrama – Data, AI, Formats and Audiences: China and Beyond brings together executives from Mango TV, FlickReels and Vigloo to discuss the $18 billion shortdrama market, while Next Foundation gathers voices from technology, policy and academia, including the National IT Industry Promotion Agency, to weigh questions around independent AI foundation models, AI assets, and IP and copyright in an era of AI transformation. InnoAsia 2026 will run Oct. 10-13, at Exhibition Center 2, BEXCO in Busan, alongside the 31st Busan International Film Festival, which runs Oct. 6-15, and the 21st Asian Contents & Film Market, held Oct. 10-13. title: Marlo Miazga Launches M Media With CBC Order For “Deeply Personal” Doc ‘Ground Control’
full_text: Skip to main content By Jesse Whittock Jesse Whittock International TV Co-Editor @WhittockTweets More Stories By Jesse British Hulu Original ‘Raising Chelsea’ Returning For Second Season On Disney+ Marlo Miazga Launches M Media With CBC Order For “Deeply Personal” Doc ‘Ground Control’ ‘Sweetpea’: Ella Purnell Is Back In Killer Role In Trailer For Season 2 Of Sky And Starz Comedy-Drama View All August 26, 2026 12:00am Marlo Miazga M Media EXCLUSIVE: Canadian producer and showrunner Marlo Miazga is launching a production company with a “deeply personal” documentary for CBC about her death of her teenage child. M Media will operate out of Toronto, as a IP-focused media business making scripted and unscripted content, with former Sphere Media boss Miazga at the helm. Miazga’s debut commission, Ground Control , is a feature documentary that has been in development alongside a memoir she is writing for Random House Canada titled Ground Control : Losing My Child to Suicide . The book, co-written with journalist Katrina Onstad, details her tragic story of losing Miazga’s 14-year-old child, Mars, to suicide in 2020 and the aftermath. Related Stories News 'Son Of A Critch': Trailer For Final Season Of Canadian Sitcom Sees Mark Having A Midlife Crisis At 17 Casting Assaad Bouab & Caroline Dhavernas Join CBC's 'Saint-Pierre'; First Look At Season 3 Canadian pubcaster CBC has now greenlit production. This will begin in October with delivery aligned for spring next year following the official launch of the book on January 26, 2027. Production finance is in place with Telefilm Canada’s Theatrical Documentary Program, the Canada Media Fund’s POV program and the Roger Documentary Fund all contributing. Watch on Deadline Directing the film is Chase Joynt ( No Ordinary Man ), with Greg Beer and Onstad the writers. Miazga will be joined as an executive producer by Catalyst founder Julie Bristow, who is a long-time colleague and an advocate for mental health, with Ryan Dias also an exec. Ground Control will have a theatrical run in Canada, which is being handled by Eyesteel Films. Worldwide rights are being shopped. Miazga is one of Canada’s premiere producers, and was most recently President and exec producer at Sphere Media’s Unscripted and Kids & Family arms. At Sphere, she oversaw docs such as Monkey on a Stick: Murder, Madness and the Hare Krishnas , an adaptation of Anne Allan’s book Dancing with Diana: A Memoir and a doc series based on Sophie Grégoire Trudeau’s memoir-cum-manifesto Closer Together: Knowing Ourselves, Loving Each Other. Return to entrepreneurial roots The launch of M returns Miazga to her entrepreneurial roots, having co-founder her first company, NewroadMedia, in 2011 with CBC exec Ann Marie Redmond. She went on to work with Bristow, another former CBC exec, at Bristow Global Media (BGM), where she developed, created and produced several shows. BGM was ultimately sold to Kew Media, and later became part of Sphere (then Datsit Sphere) when Kew went into administration over six years ago. She left Sphere in July last year, at which point she began work on her new venture. “As M Media officially launches, the greenlight for Ground Control marks a deeply personal and professional turning point,” said Miazga. “After this period of reflection and planning, I’ve built the foundations of a company rooted in resilience, creativity, and ethical storytelling. “We know how to make great shows, that has been proven countless times. The secret now is how to make them whilst experimenting, learning, adapting and remaining open, curious and kind. title: Motherhood Horror Film ‘Vagina Dentata,’ ‘From The Eclipse’ Director Nataša Urban, Boarded by Romanian Partner Manifest Film (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 25, 2026 11:57pm PT Motherhood Horror Film ‘Vagina Dentata,’ ‘From The Eclipse’ Director Nataša Urban, Boarded by Romanian Partner Manifest Film (EXCLUSIVE) Closed ahead of a Haugesund Pitch, ‘Virginia Dentata’ has also signed up Dana Bunescu, editor of ‘4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days’ By Davide Abbatescianni Plus Icon Davide Abbatescianni Latest Italian Movie Business Seeks to Build on Growth at Berlin’s European Film Market 3 years ago Jim Lee, Chief Creative Officer of DC Comics, on Finding a Work-Life Balance: ‘I Fell Asleep Twice While I Was Driving’ 3 years ago ‘300,’ ‘Sin City’ Creator Frank Miller on Setting Up His Own Publishing Banner: ‘It’s Time to Be an Adult’ 3 years ago See All 'Vagina Dentata' Courtesy of Medieoperatørene “Vagina Dentata,” the new film from Norwegian filmmaker Nataša Urban , whose “The Eclipse” won top honors at CPH:DOX in 2022, has been boarded by Manifest Film . The Romanian outfit will co-produce “Vagina Dentata,” a genre-bending exploration of motherhood and postnatal depression that will be pitched at this week’s Nordic Co-Production Market in Haugesund . Produced by Ingvil Giske through Norway’s Medieoperatørene , the project is currently 60% financed, with most of the secured funding coming from the Norwegian Film Institute. In another addition to the film, Romanian editor Dana Bunescu — whose credits include Cristian Mungiu’s “4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days,” Cristi Puiu’s “The Death of Mr. Lăzărescu,” Călin Peter Netzer’s “Child’s Pose” and Alexander Nanau’s Oscar-nominated documentary “Collective” — is attached to edit. Popular on Variety The team is now seeking additional co-production partners in France, Germany and/or Hungary, alongside further financing, distribution and festival connections. “Vagina Dentata” is one of 21 projects being presented at the Nordic Co-Production Market, part of New Nordic Films during the Norwegian International Film Festival in Haugesund , which runs this week. Urban said the film was born out of the gap between cultural expectations surrounding motherhood and her own experience after becoming a parent. “When I became a mother, what I experienced was in no way what I had been told it would be like. Instead of sunshine and butterflies, all I could think about was death,” she said. “I was terrified — a feeling that is the baseline and driving force of this film, one that I hope many others will recognize.” The project uses horror and darkly comic genre elements to approach the psychological pressures of motherhood, extending Urban’s interest in personal experience as a route into broader social and political terrain. For Giske, “Vagina Dentata” also marks another collaboration with Urban after their previous work together. “It is such a pleasure working with Nataša again, her films are both wild, funny, serious and beautiful,” Giske said. “I feel there is a need to get more diverse stories about motherhood and Haugesund as a relatively small venue is the perfect place to meet with potential collaborators.” Giske added that previous trips to Haugesund had produced partnerships the company had not originally anticipated. “Last time I was here, we set up a co-production with a country I did not initially intend to work with, so I am really looking forward to seeing what will happen this time.” The Nordic Co-Production Market brings together Nordic and international producers, financiers, distributors and sales agents around projects in development. For “Vagina Dentata,” the immediate goal is to use the market to close the remaining financing and expand the project’s European co-production structure ahead of production. title: Vidio Teams With ReelShort for First Indonesian Short-Drama Partnership
full_text: Aug 25, 2026 11:36pm PT Vidio Teams With ReelShort for First Indonesian Short-Drama Partnership By Naman Ramachandran Plus Icon Naman Ramachandran Latest Korea’s DRX Signs Strategic Partnership With Indonesia’s Nuon to Expand Gaming and Entertainment Ties (EXCLUSIVE) 2 hours ago Oscars: Japan Selects ‘All of a Sudden’ for International Feature Race 2 hours ago Vidio Teams With ReelShort for First Indonesian Short-Drama Partnership 3 hours ago See All Vidio/ReelShort Indonesian streaming platform Vidio has partnered with ReelShort , the microdrama platform owned by Crazy Maple Studio, marking ReelShort’s first entry into the Indonesian market. Hundreds of ReelShort titles will become available on Vidio starting Sept. 1. The content will stream through a dedicated Short Drama tab, accessible to subscribers on Vidio’s TV Extra, Platinum, Platinum Extra and Ultimate packages. The catalog spans genres such as fantasy, family drama, romance and billionaire romance, told in episodes running 60-90 seconds. More than 200 titles will launch with Indonesian dubbing, with a wider slate available in Indonesian subtitles. Related Stories Netflix Developing New York Yankees Drama Series From Jason Bateman, MLB and Josh Wakely Shonda Rhimes Renews Netflix Overall Deal for Another Five Years Beyond distribution, the deal includes a co-production slate between ReelShort and Indonesian production houses, with resulting series set to appear on both platforms. The partnership is also framed as a skills exchange, giving Indonesian creative talent exposure to ReelShort’s production pipeline. The agreement was brokered by AR Global Media Network. Popular on Variety The Vidio tie-up extends ReelShort’s Southeast Asian expansion after earlier partnerships in Thailand with AIS and in the Philippines with Globe. According to Media Partners Asia (MPA), ReelShort holds an estimated 29% share of global short-form drama revenue. Vidio’s Short Drama section has existed on the platform since last year. Vidio closed the second quarter of 2026 with 5.8 million paying subscribers in Southeast Asia, the third-largest total in the region. MPA data cited identifies Indonesia as Asia-Pacific’s biggest market for short-form drama viewership, representing 39% of the region’s audience, while mobile ad company Mintegral has recorded quarterly growth of 50%-200% for short-form drama apps since the third quarter of 2023. “Vidio continues to evolve alongside the changing ways Indonesians consume entertainment,” said Sutanto Hartono, CEO of Vidio. “As audiences increasingly look for content that fits seamlessly into their daily lives, we want to ensure they can find every type of entertainment they love on a single platform, from live sports, local originals, global entertainment to now, the rapidly growing format of short dramas. Our partnership with ReelShort not only responds to this emerging audience demand but also strengthens Vidio’s position as Indonesia’s most comprehensive entertainment platform, offering more choice, greater convenience, and an even richer viewing experience for our subscribers.” Crazy Maple Studio founder and CEO Joey Jia called the deal a milestone for the company’s regional strategy, saying it reflects a shift in how audiences consume entertainment as microdramas move toward the mainstream. “Indonesia is one of the region’s most dynamic entertainment markets,” Jia said. “We see tremendous potential not only to expand access to our global catalogue, but also to create original stories for Indonesian audiences. Through our planned local productions with Vidio and Indonesian production partners, we look forward to combining ReelShort’s global experience in developing high-performing short-drama IP with local creative talent to build stories and franchises that resonate locally while reaching audiences across the region and beyond.” Vidio’s move builds on its existing lead in Indonesia’s subscription video market. Per the MPA and AMPD Online Video Consumer Insights: Southeast Asia Q2 2026 report, Vidio holds the largest share of Indonesia’s SVOD subscriptions, at 20.7%. MPA CEO and executive director Vivek Couto pointed to that scale as central to Vidio’s standing in a crowded field. “Indonesia is one of the most competitive streaming markets in Southeast Asia, with strong demand for both local and international content,” Couto said. “Vidio’s position as the platform with the largest share of SVOD subscriptions in Indonesia, at 20.7%, reflects its ability to build scale through a deep understanding of the local market, supported by strong local content and engagement across categories. This position also highlights the increasingly important role of local platforms in shaping the streaming landscape across Southeast Asia.” Thousands of ReelShort episodes will be accessible on Vidio’s Short Drama tab starting Sept. 1.
