title: LevelK Boards Haugesund-Bound Norwegian Psycho Thriller ‘Anathema,’ About Repression, Denial and Collective Madness (EXCLUSIVE)
full_text: Aug 25, 2026 11:30pm PT LevelK Boards Haugesund-Bound Norwegian Psycho Thriller ‘Anathema,’ About Repression, Denial and Collective Madness (EXCLUSIVE) The film is produced by ‘No Paradise If You are Killed by a Woman’’s Janne Hjeltnes and Anne Borgaard Sørensen By Annika Pham Plus Icon Annika Pham Latest ‘Cairo Conspiracy’s’ Tawfeek Barhom to Star in Les Valseurs’ ‘Borderline’ by Oscar-Nominated Yves Piat (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago ‘Game of Thrones’ Star Kristofer Hivju Turns to Rom-Com With ‘True Love’ by ‘Little Did I Know’s’ Martina Haag (EXCLUSIVE) 2 days ago Icelandic Producer Hlín Jóhannsdóttir Sets ‘Just a Kid’ With Alief Ahead of Haugesund and Reunites With ‘Driving Mum’ Team (EXCLUSIVE) 5 days ago See All Directors Ea Johanne Sandberg (left) and Alpha Nord (right) Courtesy of Empathitude Pictures Copenhagen-based sales and aggregation outlet LevelK has boarded the Norwegian psycho-thriller “Anathema” by promising directing duo Ea Johanne Sandberg and Alpha Nord. One of 21 projects in development to be pitched today at the Nordic Co-Production Market in Haugesund, “Anathema” is being shepherded by the seasoned Janne Hjeltnes (Netflix’s “ Royalteen ,” “Midsummer Night”) and Anne Borgaard Sørensen (“Camino”, “Bullshit”), also credited respectively as producer and executive producer of the Venice-bound “ No Paradise If You Are Killed by a Woman .” Related Stories Netflix FTX Series ‘The Altruists’ Sets November Release Date, Drops First Look Photos Netflix Sets U.S. Release Date for Danny Boyle's Tabloid Drama 'Ink,' Unveils First Look at Guy Pearce as Rupert Murdoch (EXCLUSIVE) Penned by Sandberg and Nord, “Anathema” is billed as a “visceral, unsettling exploration of repression, denial and collective madness.” The central character Dafne, lives in a valley with her mother and Bror. When he vanishes, she begins to question if she or her community is falling apart. His eventual return, drowned and dead, pushes the town into full‑scale delusion: no one admits his zombie-like state and everyone insists on celebrating his wedding, even if it means sacrificing his fiancée. Popular on Variety “Dafne combines the truth-telling clarity of the boy in “The Emperor’s New Clothes” with the reluctant awakening of Neo in “The Matrix ,” said the co-directors whose graduation short “Liminal Space” was selected for the New York City Independent Film Festival in 2025. “What excited us about the project was the fresh take on a known genre and the guts of the two young female directors to approach taboo subjects in an unconventional manner and thereby mark their debut with a clear ‘what the f ***’ film which will have people do a double take,” commented Natascha Degnova, LevelK’s head of PR and marketing. She added: “This is the kind of project that fits very well into our strategy of including more genre titles to our slate, as well as of getting involved in projects before production, having a full journey and collaboration with the filmmakers from script to worldwide release.” “Anathema” is also the first feature under Hjeltnes and Sørensen’s banner Empathitude Pictures, set up in 2025 between Oslo and Copenhagen. “It’s exactly the kind of film we want to champion: character-driven, boundary-pushing and emotionally resonant, with a strong creative vision at its core,” said the producers, adding: “What makes the project particularly exciting to us is that it represents an extraordinary Gen Z approach to storytelling and filmmaking: instinctive, genre-fluid and unafraid of breaking with convention. It is the kind of filmmaking that does not simply work within an existing cinematic language but actively pushes it forward and expands what contemporary cinema can be.” The project’s film financing is being structured so far as a three-way co-production between Empathitude Pictures in Norway and Denmark and Junafilm in Germany, with funding from the Norwegian Film Institute. “It’s a low budget film [around $1.7 million] but it needs the right partners as we want those trailblazing Gen Z filmmakers to fulfil their vision,” the former Viaplay and The Global Ensemble Drama top executive Sørensen told Variety . At the Norwegian Film Festival’s industry sidebar New Nordic Films , currently underway, the Empathitude Pictures co-heads are looking for further co-financiers and distributors for “Anathema” and for their overall film and series slate. “With Anne, since launching Empathitude Pictures, we’ve been working relentlessly on our development slate, which was awarded Creative Media support this summer, so it feels like we have taken some good choices. Starting a new company these days is not easy, but we’re optimistic,” offered Hjeltnes who’s also thrilled to attend the Venice Film Festival with the world premiere – out of competition – of Halkawt Mustafa’s “ No Paradise if You Are Killed by a Woman ,” produced by Hene Films. “I have been a producer alongside Halkawt for a decade, having produced as well his previous film “ Hiding Saddam Hussein ” [an IDFA world premiere in 2023]. “This is a dream come true,” she said. New Nordic Films closes Aug. 27 and the Norwegian Intl. Film Festival in Haugesund on Aug. 28. title: Iowa MAGA AG Wants To Take California & Rob Bonta To Supreme Court Over Paramount-WBD Antitrust Suit, Maybe
full_text: Skip to main content By Dominic Patten Dominic Patten Executive Editor, Legal, Labor & Politics @DeadlineDominic More Stories By Dominic Iowa MAGA AG Wants To Take California & Rob Bonta To Supreme Court Over Paramount-WBD Antitrust Suit, Maybe Taylor Swift Praises The Late Great Dolly Parton’s Life & Legacy: “She Was Truly The Gift That Kept On Giving” Bonta Cancels Paramount Settlement Meeting; CA AG Accuses Ellison Of “Playing Games” In WBD Merger Talks View All August 25, 2026 10:09pm Paramount and Warner Bros. Towers Getty Images With friends like Iowa Attorney General Brenna Bird, does Paramount and David Ellison really need enemies? In an op-ed penned for the conservative Daily Wire Tuesday, the Hawkeye State ally of Donald Trump is threatening to take California to the Supreme Court . Declaring that “California is once again trying to be the country’s regulator,” Bird wants to stop the antitrust lawsuit from the Golden State, New York and 10 other states against Paramount’s $111 billion purchase of Warner Brothers Discovery. “Just like California should keep its hands off America’s bacon, California needs to understand that it doesn’t get to decide what Americans can choose to watch or stream,” the reelection seeking Bird states of the state and its AG Rob Bonta . Related Stories News Donald Trump Pays Tribute To Dolly Parton, Says He's Lowering U.S. Flags To Honor Entertainer News Rob Bonta Says No Paramount-WBD Settlement Talks Scheduled After He Canceled Monday Session “If California believes a transaction that 68 regulators approved is nevertheless illegal, it is free to make that argument,” she notes, lamenting the $7 million a day ticking fee and more Paramount will have to start paying WBD shareholders starting October 1. “But it should make it in the one court with the authority to bind all of us, and it should make it now, before the bill for the delay comes due,” Bird claps, leaving out any reference to the Empire State’s Letitia James and other AG. Watch on Deadline Yet, for all her rallying to the ParaBros cause, as well as some variations on what Bonta and gang are actually alleging in the March 2, 2027 trial starting case before a federal judge in Oakland, Bird doesn’t seem to have actually filed anything with SCOTUS . It also seems hard to see how even if Iowa did take California to the conservative majority Supreme Court, how they could get a hearing before next spring or even October, with the John Roberts-led high court not back in session until October 5. However, let’s sidestep Bird getting a perch on SCOTUS’ fast tracked interim relief docket (AKA the emergency docket or shadow docket) for a second, and look at a possible route under the provisions of Article III, Section 2 of the Constitution. Even if the case fell within the “original jurisdiction” criteria and passed muster with the Justices, any ruling would likely still be drawn out — likely beyond the March 2027 trial already on the calendar. In the rare case SCOTUS picks up such a state to state battle, it would generally appoint a “special master’ to review the matter before getting directly on it. All of which, like Paramount CEO Ellison accused Bonta in an August 4 NYT op-ed , makes Bird’s flag planter reek of politics. Bird, who filed a brief in 2024 support of the former Apprentice host’s ultimately successful bid to gain significant immunity from prosecution for acts taken while POTUS, sidesteps most of the meat of the actual antitrust suit the 12 states and the WGA are pursuing. A suit that Bonta, in an August 10 guest column for Deadline , paints as “a straight up antitrust enforcement case. One that is very cut and dry.” Instead, Bird, while giving the DOJ the benefit of the doubt, moves to blast Bonta and colleagues as “more hostile to this pro-competition merger than Europe and China.” The ‘To Save American Movies, I’m Taking California To The Supreme Court’ entitled piece in the Ben Shapiro-founded outlet insists a ParaBros combo is good for high streaming subscription paying Iowans, competition and the movie and TV businesses. “The merger could create a company to compete: an estimated $6 billion in savings to reinvest, and a public commitment to release at least 30 movies in theaters every year. More movies mean more entertainment — and more competition means lower prices,” Bird says. There is no mention by Bird of the $80 billion debt load a ParaBros will carry, the ongoing blame game settlement talks (or lack thereof) skirmish , nor the $1.88 billion bond Paramount desires to offset the “extraordinary losses” the court challenge poses. Bird also makes no mention of possible layoffs or other cuts from a Paramount and WBD melding. Cuts that every such M&A deal has seen. Cuts that the likes of the WGA SAG-AFTRA and theTeamsters warn of. Cut that reports in both late June and last week to the LA County Board of Supervisors warned could see thousands pink slipped, and cost the region billions in wage and hundreds of millions in tax revenue. L-R: Rob Bonta and David Ellison Getty Images Touting a Hollywood that few who live here may recognize, the Iowa AG chooses echoes the findings of earlier this year from Trump’s DOJ approving the merger. To that, right now, she says “more movies are being made, and more workers are being hired.” While seemingly concurrently stressing that a joint “Paramount+ and HBO Max together are smaller than Netflix, smaller than Disney and smaller than Amazon,” Bird also throws out there that “a successful Paramount-Warner Bros. merger would change that.” Later in the op-ed, the long time pol says: “That is the opposite of a monopoly problem.” Singing the tunes of the growing MAGA chorus that seeks to turn Bonta into the new Nancy Pelosi punching bag, Bird asserts “California is just dreaming up something radical” to go to war with Trump and his admitted “good friends” David Ellison and his Oracle founding father Larry Ellison . “California argues that the Department of Justice waved this through as a political favor to Paramount’s owners,” Bird wrote Tuesday in a smudging of what is actually in the July 13 filing by the colalition of blue states. Then someone should explain how the Department managed to get approval in China, Europe, Canada, and the other 60-plus jurisdictions. When regulators in 68 jurisdictions with different laws, different politics, and no stake whatsoever in American elections all reach the same conclusion, the outlier is not the consensus.” Again, no filing seems to have occurred today so far at the Supreme Court from Iowa or Bird. Rob Bonta and Brenna Bird’s office do share the fact that neither of them responded to Deadline’s request for comment on the Iowa AG’s threat. title: Haim Saban, Lawrence Bender and Teddy Schwarzman Among Industry Group Accusing Mark Ruffalo of “Antisemitism” in Attack on Paramount Leadership
full_text: × Skip to main content By Abid Rahman Plus Icon Abid Rahman International Editor, Digital gentlemanabroad Follow Sign Up View All August 25, 2026 9:31pm Mark Ruffalo Monica Schipper/Getty Images An entertainment industry group that includes Hollywood producers Haim Saban , Lawrence Bender and Teddy Schwarzman has released a statement condemning the alleged “antisemitic tropes” underpinning Mark Ruffalo ‘s opposition to Paramount’s leadership amid its proposed merger with Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD). The statement comes from a group calling itself The Brigade, which describes itself as “a group of nearly 1,000 members, friends, and allies of the Jewish community who are proud to be working in film, television, music, Broadway, social and digital, and other platforms in and around the entertainment industry.” Related Stories News Hannah Einbinder Defends Mark Ruffalo From Paramount "Antisemitism" Claim: "All of Us Artists Could Stand to Be More Like Mark" Business Simon Wiesenthal Center CEO Calls Out Mark Ruffalo's Paramount Remarks: "Obsession and Demonization" As well as Power Rangers media mogul Saban, Reservoir Dogs and Pulp Fiction producer Bender and Black Bear founder and CEO Schwarzman, the Brigade includes amongst its ranks Ram Bergman, Matti Leshem, Anthony Bregman, Micah Green and Lynn Harris. The Brigade’s statement comes in the wake of Ruffalo’s Aug. 21 Instagram post that spotlighted Oracle’s ties to the Israeli military — specifically a viral clip of former Oracle CEO Safra Catz at the Israeli-American Council National Summit in 2024 as it related to Israel’s war effort in Gaza. “Singling out Jewish executives and describing them in terms lifted from centuries-old antisemitic conspiracy theories, while invoking Israel as the frame for that attack, is antisemitic,” reads the statement. “It is unacceptable to introduce Jews, antizionism, or antisemitism into conversations about business transactions, simply because those involved are Jewish.” Ruffalo has long opposed both the Paramount-WBD merger over concerns about Hollywood jobs and has also long campaigned for Palestinian rights and condemned Israel’s actions in Gaza and the West Bank. The actor’s post called out Oracle founder Larry Ellison, Paramount’s controlling shareholder through a family trust, and the father of Paramount CEO David Ellison. Larry Ellison is also the key financial backstop behind Paramount’s merger attempt with WBD. The statement added: “This is a callous continuation of the ongoing campaign by the same individuals and groups targeting Jewish people and the state of Israel, a pattern of antisemitism and misinformation that puts our community in grave danger.” After Ruffalo’s initial Instagram post, a Paramount spokesperson issued a reply to the four-time Oscar-nominated and two-time Emmy-winning actor that called for the temperature of the debate around the WBD deal to be lowered and characterized Ruffalo’s remarks as “antisemitic.” In a viral X post, Ruffalo fired back that the “accusation that I am antisemitic is appalling and fundamentally dishonest.” The Brigade joins the Simon Wiesenthal Center in condemning Ruffalo’s Paramount posts. But in her own statement , Emmy-winning Hacks actress Hannah Einbinder described the “antisemitism” claims against Ruffalo as “ludicrous,” and implored more in Hollywood to “be more like Mark.” Read the full statement from The Brigade below: We are writing on behalf of a group of nearly 1000 members, friends, and allies of the Jewish community who are proud to be working in film, television, music, Broadway, social and digital, and other platforms in and around the entertainment industry. It is unfortunate that we are yet again forced to state our unequivocal condemnation of the use of antisemitic tropes and narratives by those who use their platform for targeted hate speech toward Jews. Singling out Jewish executives and describing them in terms lifted from centuries-old antisemitic conspiracy theories, while invoking Israel as the frame for that attack, is antisemitic. It is unacceptable to introduce Jews, antizionism, or antisemitism into conversations about business transactions, simply because those involved are Jewish. There is nothing “strange” about a Jewish executive discussing substantive issues about tech. This is not commentary on a merger. It is not a criticism of a government. It is simple antisemitism, where Jewish executives are portrayed as a secretive and powerful wealth-hoarding elite delighting in mass death. This is the same rhetoric that Nazis, Soviets, and the Klan weaponized against Jews, and its consequences are not only historical: they show up today in attacks against Jews in our streets, our synagogues, and our schools. This is a callous continuation of the ongoing campaign by the same individuals and groups targeting Jewish people and the state of Israel, a pattern of antisemitism and misinformation that puts our community in grave danger. There is no excuse and no defense for this rhetoric, including the “I have Jewish friends” rationale, and there are many questions that demand an answer — including, is there someone behind the funding of this campaign that is continuously perpetrated by the same individuals? We will keep standing up against this hatred. Because when we say, NEVER AGAIN, we mean it. THR

title: Dolly Parton, a Hollywood Treasure Who Lit Up the Screen With Her Authentic Self
full_text: Skip to main content By David Rooney Plus Icon David Rooney Chief Film Critic DavidCRooney1 Follow Sign Up View All August 25, 2026 7:58pm From left: Lily Tomlin, Dolly Parton and Jane Fonda in '9 to 5.' 20th Century Fox Film Corp./Courtesy Everett Collection When Jane Fonda was developing the rollicking 1980 workplace farce 9 to 5 , inspired by a real-life women’s rights organization of that name, at some point the project shape-shifted from the serious drama that was originally planned to a comedy, enlisting the brilliant Colin Higgins to direct and work on the screenplay with Patricia Resnick. Having cast Lily Tomlin as her acerbic ally in the secretarial pool, Fonda and producer Bruce Gilbert wanted to broaden the film’s appeal, landing on the idea of a third lead who might push beyond urban liberals to reach mainstream, conservative and Southern audiences. From that commercially-driven demographic strategy, Dolly Parton the Movie Star was born. Related Stories Movies James Lew, Stuntman and 'Hot Shots! Part Deux' Actor, Dies at 73 Movies Rene Malo, 'Decline of the American Empire' Producer, Dies at 84 As Doralee Rhodes, the happily married secretary of Dabney Coleman’s lecherous corporate vice president, kept busy dodging his unwelcome advances, Parton was a natural. Her luminosity, effervescence, folksy delivery and innate comic timing infused the film with livewire energy, whether she was fantasizing about hog-tieing and spit-roasting the boss or bringing that fantasy to life, like a seasoned rodeo queen. The movie became a massive hit, grossing more than $103 million at a time when a women-centric, empowerment-minded blockbuster was almost unimaginable. Every one of the predominantly female ensemble comedies that became pop cultural fixtures in later decades — The First Wives Club , Sister Act , The Devil Wears Prada , Bridesmaids — owes 9 to 5 a debt. The eternally catchy country pop theme song Parton wrote and recorded for the film left its own mark, reaching number one on Billboard ’s Country, Hot 100 and Adult Contemporary charts. Parton often said in interviews that she came up with the song’s tapping typewriter-key rhythm by clicking her long acrylic fingernails together. The death of a global superstar is invariably a sad event, but the loss of Parton today at age 80 is an uncommonly crushing blow to many of us. For gay men, she was our North Star, a beacon of inclusivity in a world of persistent intolerance. Her theme park near the Great Smoky Mountains, Dollywood, was a pilgrimage destination on the queer-tourism map. If gays ran the Oval Office, her birthday would be a national holiday. Parton frequently mined self-deprecating humor from her almost cartoonish appearance — the boobs, the big blonde wigs, the bejeweled outfits, the cosmetic surgeries — and yet she remained unequivocally real. I saw her perform just once at a Radio City Music Hall concert in 2005 as part of her Vintage Tour, along with a sea of gay men who had resurrected their Westernwear from Madonna’s “Don’t Tell Me” period for the occasion. When an elaborate piece of stage scenery malfunctioned and failed to descend from the flies during her opening number, Parton quipped that a little old country girl from East Tennessee should never have even attempted something so fancy. The iconic look and larger-than-life persona were an inextricable part of her sui generis screen presence in a handful of beloved movies. She was never an actress with significant range, but the thing is, she never had to be. The sweetness, the sense of humor and the old-fashioned goodness that epitomized who she was in her many walks of life made her incandescent. From her very first entrance, we knew exactly who her character was, almost all of them a mirror to who Parton was in real life. In The Best Little Whorehouse in Texas , starring as Miss Mona Stangley alongside Burt Reynolds, she made being the madam of a brothel — or as she puts it in one of her songs, “A Lil’ Ole Bitty Pissant Country Place” — seem wholesome, caring for her “girls” like they were her own children. Rewatching that cornbread musical in a Houston gay bar in the early ‘80s was a hootenanny I’ll never forget, Stetsons constantly flying up in the air in jubilant appreciation. In Steel Magnolias , an all-star tear-jerker about the fortitude to be drawn from female friendship in times of sadness, Parton played the big-haired, open-hearted small-town Louisiana beauty parlor owner, Truvy Jones. (Her character names alone are divine.) Her salon was a social hub, a place for harmless gossip and friendly banter, and a respite for its regulars from their frequently exasperating husbands and sons. Watching Parton hold her own alongside pros like Sally Field, Olympia Dukakis and Shirley MacLaine was bliss, not to mention seeing her character in a loving marriage with the coolest — OK, and sexiest — of modern-day cowboys, Sam Shepard. It’s doubtful that anyone would try to make a case for the 1984 Sylvester Stallone vehicle, Rhinestone ; I wonder if there’s even a living soul who managed to get through it. But Parton could sew a silk purse out of a sow’s ear, introducing two top 10 country hits in the movie. Her gifts were put to more memorable use in the cheesy but disarming comedy Straight Talk , as Shirlee Kenyon, a Southern transplant looking to rebuild her life in Chicago, where she becomes an accidental talk radio call-in advice show host. And Parton brought her signature warmth and wit to the guilty pleasure Joyful Noise , playing G.G. Sparrow, a feisty widow wrestling for control of her small Georgia town’s choir with Queen Latifah’s Vi Rose Hill. When Vi Rose gets her in a headlock, G.G. squawks, “Oow, you’re breakin’ my hair!” Putting aside her many cameos and popular TV movies, Parton’s filmography was by most standards meager. But she inhabited every role with spirit, vigor, compassion and charm for days, qualities entirely true to herself. Her death leaves the world a much poorer place. THR

title: Taylor Swift Remembers Dolly Parton’s “True Grace and Grit”: “Her Legacy Will Be Everlasting”
full_text: × Skip to main content By McKinley Franklin Plus Icon McKinley Franklin View All August 25, 2026 7:56pm Getty Taylor Swift is honoring the late country music icon Dolly Parton . Parton died Tuesday in Nashville at 80, her family announced. She died after a “brief battle with cancer,” her reps told People . “A world without Dolly doesn’t feel possible, real, or right,” Swift began in a statement shared with The Hollywood Reporter . “But because of the eternally generous way she spent her time on this earth and the countless lives she changed for the better, her legacy will be an everlasting one.” Related Stories Music Beyoncé Remembers Dolly Parton as "Bold and Brilliant" in Touching Tribute TV '20/20' Sets Dolly Parton Special Tribute: Where to Watch Online “She was truly the gift that kept on giving. Dolly gave us someone to look up to while encouraging us to be who we are as individuals. Somehow she was able to give us her lessons about the world gently and honestly, simultaneously, and oftentimes hilariously,” Swift continued. “She managed to give the world the ultimate mystery and fantasy in some corners of her life, but to give full transparency in the ways that counted. Somehow she was true grace and true grit, all in one dazzling person. She possessed the softest heart when it came to the struggles of others, and a backbone of steel to defend her own self worth as an artist.” She concluded, “Along with her other fans, I am so grateful for all of it. For the melodies and lyrics she wrote that thawed even the coldest hearts. For the millions of books she provided children all over the world so that they might fall in love with stories the way she did. For the tightropes she walked so that young girls like me could grow up dreaming of joining the circus too. Dolly, I’ll think of you each step of the way.” Last September, the “Jolene” singer announced she was postponing a set of Las Vegas concerts to deal with “some health challenges.” In May, she canceled her Las Vegas residency, but continued to put on a brave front, telling her fans that she was OK. In July, just ahead of her Madison Square Garden wedding, Swift and Travis Kelce donated $26 million to varying organizations, including to Dolly Parton”s Imagination Library. Parton shared an Instagram video thanking the married couple for their donation, where she said she was “blown away and overjoyed with that gratitude.” “Now, it’s evident, that you have made giving back a key part of your lives, so hey, when you have you firstborn, can I have it?” she joked. “Because that is gonna be one special baby!” The 14-time Grammy Award winner also reflected on the two-time Oscar nominee’s legacy in Parton’s 2023 profile with The Hollywood Reporter . “Dolly is a force of evolution and transformation in our industry, but she does it with such playful levity it almost looks effortless. Her sense of humor and mischief are easily my favorite things about her, because I think it forces the world to reconcile that a woman can be a serious artist and writer who also has raucous fun with it, can make people laugh and be in on every joke,” Swift told THR . “She’s never stopped challenging herself to clear new hurdles and explore new territory artistically, and I think that speaks to her great curiosity about the human condition. She’s a legendary empath and the storyteller for the ages. She’s also having the most fun doing it.” THR

title: Jelly Roll Takes Jabs at Donald Trump While Guest Hosting ‘Jimmy Kimmel Live!’
full_text: Skip to main content By Carly Thomas Plus Icon Carly Thomas Senior Editor, Digital carly_thomas_ Follow Sign Up View All August 25, 2026 7:42pm Jelly Roll on 'Jimmy Kimmel Live!' Disney Logo text During Jelly Roll ‘s return as guest host of Jimmy Kimmel Live! on Monday night , the country singer took several opportunities to throw jabs at President Donald Trump . During his opening monologue, the country singer-rapper started with the “main event of America this weekend” — the IndyCar race in Washington, D.C., dubbed the Freedom 250 Grand Prix. “The cars drove through the streets of D.C., and there’s Donald Trump, who apparently has never held a flag before,” he said, as a video played of the president waving a green flag. “What a shit job. How do you fuck up waving a flag?” Related Stories Music Trump Orders Flags to Fly at Half-Staff in Wake of Dolly Parton's Death: "The World Loves You" TV Rosie O'Donnell Joke About Trump and Natalie Harp Draws Gasps From 'Kimmel' Crowd As the audience broke out in laughter, Jelly Roll continued, “But the president seemed to enjoy the IndyCar race, which was a real switch up for him, because normally he only likes his own race.” “Trump also drove around the track in his motorcade doing what they call the lap of honor, which sounds like a loyalty program at a strip club,” the singer quipped. “Five percent cash back in the champagne room for all Lap of Honor members. Sadly, those are the only laps Trump’s been doing lately.” Jelly Roll’s “laps” joke was only the beginning of several more digs directed at Trump’s physical fitness during the monologue. “According to the Washington Post , a lot of doctors are worried about the president’s weight. After his last physical, we found out Trump gained 14 pounds, which means he’s now tipping the scales at almost 240. It’s crazy. Think about this, y’all. In the last few years, I’ve lost 300 pounds. That means I’ve lost an entire Donald Trump,” the “Save Me” artist said, prompting laughter from the studio crowd. He added, “And let’s be honest, based on his approval ratings, it seems like most of the country wants to do the same thing.” Jelly Roll told the audience they should “take it easy” on Trump because “we shouldn’t be making fun of the president for his weight because we know that he would never do that to other people.” That’s when a video montage started to play of the president talking about people’s weight and appearance on many different occasions, calling others a “big fat slob,” “fat pig” and “fatter than ever,” among other terms. “Well, if that ain’t the pot calling the kettle fat,” the singer said. “Well, Mr. President, from one fat pig to another, take it from me that physical fitness is very important. And trust me, you’ll be happy to see your penis again.” Jelly Roll first guest hosted Jimmy Kimmel Live! in July 2025 before returning this week while regular host Jimmy Kimmel is on his summer hiatus. The country star has been open about maintaining an apolitical public stance . Despite being criticized for avoiding politics, Jelly Roll told reporters backstage at the 2026 Grammys that “people shouldn’t care” about his political opinions because “I’m a dumb redneck.” THR
